summary.headline: IHCL raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% after Q2 revenue rose 22% to INR2,484 crores and standalone EBITDA margin hit 38.9%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was strong: consolidated operating revenue grew 22% YoY to INR2,484 crores, operating EBITDA grew 24% to INR706 crores (28.4% margin, up 50 bps), and PAT rose 23% to INR349 crores. Standalone operating revenue grew 26% to INR1,336 crores and standalone EBITDA grew 40% to INR520 crores, with margin up 400 bps to 38.9%. Management raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% from 12%-14%, with Hotel segment growth of 17%-19%. Occupancy rose to 82% from 75%, and TajSATS remained a drag on margins.

financial_highlights.value: Revenue and EBITDA growth of 25% and 30%

segments.name: Hotels (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 25% and EBITDA up 30% YoY; domestic hotel RevPAR up 25% and standalone RevPAR up 28%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands.

segments.name: Management fees
segments.commentary: Income up 25% to INR156 crores, driven by 25% growth in managed room inventory, higher RevPAR, technical fees and new brand fees from branded residences and villas; management targets high-teens fee CAGR.

segments.name: Select service (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger revenue INR193 crores (+25%) at 40% EBITDA margin; Ginger reached 100 operational hotels and targets 150 by March 31, 2027. Qmin has over 130 outlets, Ama over 400 villas and bungalows, Tree of Life over 50 resorts.

segments.name: TajSATS (air catering)
segments.commentary: EBITDA declined sequentially in Q2 due to airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure; non-aviation institutional catering partly offset the decline. Management expects improvement in H2.

segments.name: International subsidiaries
segments.commentary: St. James' Court margins fell 360 bps YoY in H1 FY27 due to delayed renovation works and cost pressure; management expects London recovery with double-digit growth in October. Pierre (New York) is EBITDA-positive but not at target margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth raised to 15%-17% (from 12%-14%), i.e. 300 bps above prior guidance; Hotel segment revenue growth 17%-19%.
Implied H2 growth is well above the 14% midpoint arithmetic, per CFO, as TajSATS is a drag and H2 is seasonally strong; the guidance excludes OHL.
Plan to open 50 hotels in FY27; 30 expected in H2 (possibly 32-34). Standalone hotel count was 392 operational as of Oct 27, 2026, with 4 more openings in October.

Management to publish a revised portfolio target (700-hotel Accelerate 2030 target expected to be crossed early) by mid-November 2026; separate management-fee guidance expected by end of next quarter.
OHL merger: 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares; appointed date April 1, 2027; expected to add 6%-7% to standalone operating revenue in FY28, not in FY27 guidance.
Management expects more than INR1,000 crores of management fee income in roughly two years and about 5,000 keys opened per year.
capex_capacity: Portfolio at 670 hotels with over 69,000 keys (operational or under development) at end-H1 FY27; 47 hotels signed and 20 opened in H1 FY27.
Pipeline of over 34,800 keys, 94% capital-light (81% management contracts, 13% leases).
H1 FY27 capex is 20%-30% above the annual average of the preceding 7-8 years, per management.

Asset upgrades at Taj Palace New Delhi, President Mumbai, Taj West End Bengaluru, Taj Fort Aguada and Taj Lake Palace; Taj Palace New Delhi room revenue up 132% YoY and crossed INR100 crores monthly revenue in September.
Expected upcoming Frankfurt ramp-up after start-up challenges; London and San Francisco expected to improve in Q3.
demand_pricing: Occupancy rose to 82% from 75% in Q2 last year; standalone and domestic consolidated occupancy each up roughly 6%-7%, so growth was balanced between occupancy and ARR.
Demand supported by MICE events (BRICS Summit, Bloomberg event, fintech event); management said Q2 ex-BRICS would still have been a comfortable double-digit RevPAR number.
Wedding nights next year are expected at about 95 versus 60-65 normally, a tailwind for social MICE.
Domestic demand is the main pillar; foreign tourist arrivals have a 3.9% 10-year CAGR, and management sees upside if this reaches 5%-6%. Room nights were flat YoY in Q2 per management.

Tier 2/3 supply: management says demand growth of 15%-20% in these markets is largely met by unorganised players, and that the 12% capacity CAGR headline should be viewed with caution given project delays.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the H2 guidance implied by the revised numbers, and is occupancy at 82% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be mostly rate-led plus new hotels and international recovery (London, Pierre, San Francisco, Frankfurt), with occupancy gains also in the mix; H2 guidance is conservative given the 30-34 hotel openings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TajSATS EBITDA fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure, mainly from June; Q2 had the full impact. Non-flight catering grew, but at lower margin. FY27 is a consolidation year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% implied H2 growth conservative and what are the uplift drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H2 growth would have to be higher than the 14% arithmetic to hit guidance, given TajSATS drag, a high Q4 base and seasonally strong MICE and weddings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% growth in Q2 driven by renovation base effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renovations are routine for iconic assets; H1 capex is 20%-30% above normal and the growth reflects structural demand shifts, not only a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Why keep international assets, given lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strategic value of the global Taj brand; international consolidated margin of about 35% is stated as industry-leading, with London profitable and Pierre EBITDA-positive but not at 20%-25% margins.

qa_highlights.question: What can standalone RevPAR be without BRICS, and how sustainable is the 400 bps margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs in Q2; margin gain from operating leverage, MICE, and management fee mix (booked standalone). Management did not give specific margin guidance but expects a positive margin trend despite new payroll and regulatory costs.

risks_watch: West Asia geopolitics: higher fuel prices and airline capacity cuts hit TajSATS and international travel; Dubai and Ras Al Khaimah fees affected.
TajSATS margin recovery in H2 depends on airline schedules and West Asia developments.
International subsidiaries: St. James' Court margin decline (360 bps in H1); London renovation and property-tax effects; Pierre profitability target still unresolved.
Depreciation up about 20% YoY on consolidated basis (34% on the non-standalone line) from acquisitions and new assets; watch for margin dilution.
Pending OHL merger (close expected before April 1, 2027) and revised portfolio and management-fee guidance due mid-November 2026 and end of next quarter.
Chennai and Kolkata lag other metros on FTA-dependent demand; management expects recovery in next one or two quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, guidance and pipeline, with frank acknowledgement of TajSATS, international margins and West Asia headwinds. Management was somewhat defensive on the international portfolio and evasive on the exact H2 growth math and the Q2 ex-event RevPAR figure.
key_quotes: Accordingly, we are revising our full year growth guidance upwards to 15% to 17%.
So international is what makes Taj the world's strongest hotel brand.
I would say, optimistic on TajSATS going back to where it was and actually even improving upon it in the second half.
I think we are getting very close to finding a more sustainable solution, but this is not the one which will do 20% 25% EBITDA margin.
